title: Understanding the Minimum Casual Wage Australia: Rates, Loading, and Your Take-Home Pay
description: Learn about the minimum casual wage Australia from 1 July 2026: $33.05/hr including 25% loading. Compare award rates, super, and tax for casual employees.
salarySummary: From 1 July 2026, the minimum casual wage in Australia is $33.05 per hour, based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 plus 25% casual loading, assuming a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the minimum casual wage in Australia from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: The minimum casual wage for award/agreement-free adult employees is $33.05 per hour. This is the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour plus a 25% casual loading. Casual employees covered by an award may have different rates, often higher. Always check your award or agreement.

faqs.q: How is casual loading calculated on top of the base rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the casual loading adds $6.61, making the total $33.05. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator; instead, enter the base rate and apply the loading separately.

faqs.q: Do award rates affect the minimum casual wage?
faqs.a: Yes. Most casual employees are covered by an award, which sets minimum pay rates that can be higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award has specific rates. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator (PACT) to find the correct award rate for your job.

bodyMarkdown:
## What Is the Minimum Casual Wage Australia?

If you’re a casual employee or considering casual work, knowing the **minimum casual wage Australia** is essential. From 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission set the National Minimum Wage at $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, bringing the minimum casual rate to **$33.05 per hour**.

This rate applies to adult employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. However, most casual workers are covered by an award, which may set higher minimum rates. Always check your specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman’s tools.

### How the Minimum Casual Wage Is Calculated

The formula is straightforward:

**Casual hourly rate = Base hourly rate × (1 + 25% loading)**

For the National Minimum Wage:
- Base rate: $26.44
- Casual loading: $6.61 (25% of $26.44)
- Total casual rate: $33.05

To find your annual gross pay as a casual, multiply your casual hourly rate by hours per week and by 52 weeks. Assuming 38 hours per week:

**Annual gross = $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80**

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use our [timesheet](/) to estimate your own figures.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. But most industries have awards with higher minimum rates. For example, the *Supported Employment Services Award* and the *Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award* have their own pay structures.

Award rates often include:
- Different classifications based on skill level
- Junior rates for employees under 21
- Disability support employee rates
- Penalty rates for weekends, public holidays, or late nights

Casual loading is still applied on top of the award base rate unless the award says otherwise. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT) can help you find the exact rate for your job.

### Special Minimum Wages for Juniors, Apprentices, and Trainees

If you’re under 21, an apprentice, or a trainee, special minimum wages apply. These are percentages of the National Minimum Wage based on age or training stage. For example, a 20-year-old junior may receive 85% of the adult rate. Casual loading still applies on top of that reduced base rate. Check the National Minimum Wage Order for the exact percentages.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Casual Wage

Superannuation (super) is an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your casual wage. For the 2026–27 financial year, the super guarantee rate is 12%, with a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

Example: If you earn $33.05 per hour casual, your employer must pay an extra $3.97 per hour into your super fund. That’s $7,836.82 per year on top of your gross pay (assuming 38 hours/week).

Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it’s an additional cost to the employer. When comparing job offers, always consider the total package including super. See our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Tax on Your Casual Wage

As a casual employee, you pay income tax and the Medicare levy on your earnings. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% for each dollar over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% for each dollar over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% for each dollar over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% for each dollar over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

For a full-time casual earning $65,306.80 per year:
- Tax-free threshold: $18,200
- Tax on next $26,800 (up to $45,000): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $20,306.80 (up to $135,000): 30% = $6,092.04
- Total tax: $10,112.04
- Medicare levy (2% of $65,306.80): $1,306.14
- Total deductions: $11,418.18
- Estimated annual take-home pay: $53,888.62

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

## Fortnightly Pay: A Common Cycle for Casuals

Many casual employees are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay:

**Fortnightly gross = Weekly gross × 2**

For a minimum casual wage earner working 38 hours/week:
- Weekly gross: $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
- Fortnightly gross: $1,255.90 × 2 = $2,511.80

After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home would be approximately $2,073.80. This can help with budgeting and comparing job offers.

## How to Use the Hourly to Annual Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) is designed for casual and permanent employees. Enter your **base hourly rate** (before casual loading). If you are casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

The tool then calculates:
- Annual gross pay (hourly × hours per week × 52)
- Fortnightly and weekly amounts
- Estimated tax and Medicare
- Superannuation (12% on top)

It assumes 38 hours per week unless you change it. Remember: this is an estimate. Your actual pay may differ due to award rates, overtime, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

## Key Takeaways

- The **minimum casual wage Australia** from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour (National Minimum Wage $26.44 + 25% loading).
- Most casuals are covered by an award with higher rates. Check your award using [reference tables](/data) or the Fair Work Ombudsman.
- Super is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings.
- Tax is progressive; use our tools to estimate your take-home pay.
- Always enter your base rate (excluding casual loading) into calculators.

Understanding your minimum entitlements ensures you’re paid correctly. For more details, visit the Fair Work Ombudsman or Fair Work Commission websites.
